name: RoomUs Yokohama
card: Keikyu's work and study rooms, two minutes from the East Exit of Yokohama Station
title: RoomUs Yokohama — Keikyu's work and study rooms, two minutes from the East Exit of Yokohama Station
lead: RoomUs Yokohama, a coworking space run by Keikyu Corporation, is on the 7th floor of a building in Takashima 2-chome, a two-minute walk from the East Exit of Yokohama Station. It opened on 6 January 2025. There are four kinds of seat — private seats, semi-private seats, a café area and soundproof booths — and it is open 7:00–23:00 every day of the year. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Yokohama Station East Exit, 2 min walk
concept: A safe, comfortable third place close to home
RoomUs is Keikyu Corporation's coworking space. Under the idea of “a safe, comfortable third place close to home”, it offers quality work and study rooms at affordable prices.
It is unstaffed, and you enter with a members-only smart lock. Advance member registration is required.
steps: According to Keikyu's news release, there are eight private seats.
There are 12 semi-private seats. Together with the private seats, the layout centres on seats for working alone.
Somewhere to rest, somewhere to talk
The café area has three seats. There are two soundproof booths, bookable at ¥100 per 20 minutes.
Full-time membership is ¥18,500 a month. There are morning, day and night plans for both weekdays and holidays.
Pay-by-time use is ¥100 per 20 minutes, with a minimum charge of ¥300 a month. Lockers are ¥1,000 a month.

word.title: What is a smart lock?
body: A system that locks and unlocks a door using a smartphone or member credentials.
RoomUs is unstaffed and keeps entry and exit secure with a members-only smart lock.

credits: Keikyu Corporation (managed by R-Bank Co., Ltd.)
RoomUs Yokohama official website / Keikyu news release on the opening of RoomUs Yokohama

name: TANEMAKI
card: A coworking space for long stays, running near Yokohama Station since 2011
title: TANEMAKI — somewhere between a library and a café, eight minutes from Yokohama Station
lead: TANEMAKI is a coworking space on the ground floor of Sunny Court Yokohama in Okano, Nishi Ward, an eight-minute walk from Yokohama Station. It has been running near Yokohama Station since 2011, and the official website describes it as a space “halfway between a library and a café”. There are 18 seats plus sofas, available 24 hours. Everything below is based on the official website.
concept: Making a place where people get things done
TANEMAKI's idea is “making a place where people go and do something”. It aims to increase the number of people who turn ideas into action, and to create a lively place.
It is designed for long stays — for work, studying for qualifications or reading. Coming and going is free, talking is fine and you can bring things in.
steps: Four kinds of table, three kinds of chair
There are 18 seats plus sofas, with four kinds of table and three kinds of chair.
Every seat has a 60 W USB-C power supply, mobile cables and outlets.
There are 13 monitors, first come, first served. As well as Wi-Fi, three seats have wired LAN.
Free drinks such as tea and coffee are available, and all seats are non-smoking.
A ground floor eight minutes from Yokohama Station
It is on the ground floor of Sunny Court Yokohama, with a TANEMAKI sign at the entrance.
Drop-in costs ¥375–¥1,480 per person per hour, monthly use starts at ¥5,480, and there is no joining fee.

word.title: What is a coworking space?
body: A new kind of workplace where different people work in the same place and solve problems through exchange and cooperation.
TANEMAKI is described as valuing study sessions and events, and putting effort into building community.

credits: TANEMAKI official website: top page, “About TANEMAKI”, “Equipment”

name: M.A.D.center
card: A 7th floor in a station-front building, with murals and coffee
title: M.A.D.center — a hub with murals and a coffee counter, two minutes from the West Exit of Matsudo Station
lead: M.A.D.center is on the 7th floor of the Le Cinéma Building, a two-minute walk from the West Exit of Matsudo Station on the JR and Shin-Keisei lines. A community facility renamed from the former Matsudo shareBASE, it reopened on 25 February 2026, bringing together a coworking space, three meeting rooms and a 3D-printer studio on one floor. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR & Shin-Keisei Matsudo Station West Exit, 2 min walk
Drop-in Tue–Sat 9:00–22:00 (monthly members 24 hours every day)
Drop-in from ¥220 per 30 min, ¥1,320 per day / monthly ¥9,900 (incl. tax)
concept: A station-front shared space connected to the town's makers

M.A.D.center is a shared space run by MAD City, which works on community building around Matsudo Station. It reopened on 25 February 2026, renewed from the former Matsudo shareBASE, as a community facility with coworking, meeting rooms and a 3D-printer studio.

The official website also highlights collaboration with local creators and businesses. Mahamel Coffee, Sakura Parti and STUDIO Canvas were involved, adding green benches, colourful murals and a drinks counter from a local coffee roaster.
steps: Work seats with green benches and murals
Monthly members can use the coworking space without time limits. Drop-in runs Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00–22:00, from ¥220 per 30 minutes or ¥1,320 a day.
Green benches and colourful murals bring colour to this one floor of a station-front building.
A floor lined with work seats
A coffee counter from a local roaster
There is a drinks counter from a local coffee roaster.
Private booths are also available, so calls and online meetings can be kept separate.
The coffee counter in the coworking space
A private booth in the coworking space
The three meeting rooms are Large (14 people) and Middle and Window (6 people each). They cost ¥480–¥980 per 30 minutes, and monthly members pay half the drop-in rate.
Middle can be booked as a drop-in on Sundays and Mondays. On other days, the official website advises against confidential meetings there, as sound carries.
Two minutes from the station, 24 hours for members
Monthly members pay ¥9,900 for 24-hour access every day. The 3D printers are shown on the official website as being renewed.
Two minutes from the West Exit of Matsudo Station, it is easy to drop in from anywhere along the Joban Line.

word.title: What is MAD City?
body: A project working on community building around Matsudo Station. Its official website features several places around town, such as a studio in an old house and an event space.
M.A.D.center is one of MAD City's station-front bases, handling coworking and meeting rooms.

credits: MAD City official website: “M.A.D.center (formerly Matsudo shareBASE)”

name: Noblesse Oblige (NOB)
card: A local workplace with raised seating, eight minutes from the East Exit of Kashiwa Station
title: Noblesse Oblige (NOB) — coworking with raised seating and sofas, near the East Exit of Kashiwa Station
lead: Noblesse Oblige — NOB for short — is on the 3rd floor of the Daiichi Mitoya Building, an eight-minute walk along the station-front street from the East Exit of Kashiwa Station on the JR Joban Line and Tobu Noda Line. It combines a shared office and coworking space with rental meeting rooms and rental space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Joban Line & Tobu Noda Line Kashiwa Station East Exit, 8 min walk
8:50–22:00 (weekends & holidays 10:00–18:00; closed during the Kashiwa festival, New Year, etc.)
concept: A workplace for “local living where you know your neighbours”

Under the keyword “local living where you know your neighbours”, NOB proposes working and living close together rather than separating home and work. It aims to be a base for creators rooted in the area and for would-be entrepreneurs who want to energise their town.

Creators, entrepreneurs and remote workers use it as a workplace, and it is also used for studying for qualifications. The official website describes it as “a spacious place where you can focus on your work”.
steps: The focus desks are named on the official website as the “number one most popular” seats, for when you want to work quietly on your own.
Open 8:50–22:00 on weekdays, it is handy before work or on the way home.
Popular raised seats, sofas and high tables
The raised seating area (koagari) is also presented on the official website as popular.
There are sofa and high-table seats too, so you can choose to suit your mood or task.
From ¥400 an hour, plus monthly plans
Drop-in is ¥400 per hour or ¥1,500 per day (excl. tax). Show a student ID for a youth discount of ¥1,000 a day.
Monthly membership has five plans — G, S, W, W+ and N — from ¥11,000 to ¥35,000 a month (excl. tax; joining fee ¥5,000).

word.title: What does “working near home” mean?
body: Keeping your home and workplace close together (shokuju kinsetsu in Japanese) — the opposite of separating them and commuting into the city centre.
NOB champions this as a base for people living in Kashiwa to work locally.

name: Yu~Work (Natural Hot Spring Yu~neru)
card: Work in hot-spring loungewear, inside a bathhouse
title: Yu~Work (Natural Hot Spring Yu~neru) — a workspace inside a natural hot-spring facility, two minutes from Shin-Narashino Station
lead: The natural hot spring Yu~neru is on the 2nd floor of the Mr Max Shin-Narashino Shopping Center, a two-minute walk from Shin-Narashino Station on the JR Keiyo Line. Yu~Work is the coworking space inside it. You can do remote work and meetings in the facility's loungewear, and switch gears in the hot spring or sauna between tasks. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Keiyo Line Shin-Narashino Station, 2 min walk (parking available)
Drop-in ¥500 for 5 hours (incl. tax; bathhouse entry charged separately)
concept: Remote work and meetings in loungewear

Yu~Work is a coworking space inside the natural hot spring Yu~neru. Presenting it as “a new way of working”, the official website highlights that you can work remotely and hold meetings in the facility's loungewear.
It is a workspace for people who want to get work done, also usable for remote meetings and discussions. When you tire of work, the hot spring and sauna are in the same building.
steps: There are 8 fixed seats and 6 seats in an open space. Drop-in is ¥500 for five hours, with extensions at ¥100 per hour (incl. tax).
Bathhouse entry is charged on top: ¥1,050 on weekdays and ¥1,150 on weekends and holidays.
Hire the whole room for up to 12
With advance booking, you can hire the whole coworking room. Private hire is for up to 12 people, at ¥5,000 for three hours or ¥8,000 for five (incl. tax; book by the day before).
The official website says you can hold meetings in loungewear.
Power and USB, whiteboard, free drinks
Equipment includes a 55-inch TV, power and USB, a whiteboard, internet and lockers, and drinks are free.
That the baths themselves count among the facilities is something no other coworking space has.

word.title: What is bathhouse loungewear?
body: Comfortable clothing provided by a bathhouse for wearing inside the facility before and after bathing.
At Yu~Work, you can work remotely and hold meetings in this loungewear, moving between the hot spring and work without changing.

credits: Natural Hot Spring Yu~neru official website: “Coworking space Yu~Work”

name: Tokorozawa Node
card: Meeting rooms and a workspace, two minutes from Tokorozawa Station
title: Tokorozawa Node — a shared space aiming to be a hub for people and business, two minutes from the West Exit of Tokorozawa Station
lead: Tokorozawa Node is on the 3rd floor of Tokorozawa Sun Plaza, halfway along Prope-dori, a two-minute walk from the West Exit of Tokorozawa Station on the Seibu Ikebukuro and Shinjuku lines. It is a shared space combining rental meeting rooms, a shared office, a coworking workspace and multipurpose booths, with over 330 m² of floor space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Seibu Ikebukuro & Shinjuku lines Tokorozawa Station West Exit, 2 min walk
concept: A “node” where people and businesses cross paths
Tokorozawa Node is positioned as a facility for people who want to energise their business. It aims to be a “node (hub)” where many kinds of businesses gather and exchanges and new ideas are born.
With over 330 m² of floor space, it is presented as large for the Tokorozawa area.
steps: A semi-private workspace with a sliding door and small windows
The coworking workspace has 6 seats and holds up to 10. It is a semi-private room enclosed by walls with a sliding door and small windows.
The official website describes a new design balancing a sense of privacy with a calm environment.
There is a large meeting room (20–30 people, max 30), a medium room (max 8) and a small room (max 4). The large room comes with a big screen as standard.
Members get 20% off the standard meeting-room rate (booking required).
There is a café corner and a vending machine for anyone to use, plus fast internet, a paid multifunction printer and lockers with lockable mailboxes.
The shared office comes with a dedicated desk (110 cm × 70 cm) and business chair for ¥38,500 a month (incl. tax).

word.title: What is a node?
body: A word for a “knot” or “junction point” in something connected like a net.
Tokorozawa Node takes the name because it aims to be a hub where diverse businesses gather and interact.

credits: Tokorozawa Node official website: top page

name: Tanashi Coworking Space OK Nishitokyo
card: Coworking that supports women starting businesses, three minutes from Tanashi Station
title: Tanashi Coworking Space OK Nishitokyo — a start-up support hub three minutes from the South Exit of Tanashi Station
lead: Tanashi Coworking Space OK Nishitokyo is in an area lined with the library and city offices, a three-minute walk from the South Exit of Tanashi Station on the Seibu Shinjuku Line. A facility supporting women's first steps into starting a business, it combines coworking, a virtual office and a tourist information point for Nishitokyo City. Besides the open space, there are shared desks and two meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Seibu Shinjuku Line Tanashi Station South Exit, 3 min walk
¥500 for 2 hours, then ¥250 per hour, up to ¥1,500 per day
hero_cap: OK Nishitokyo (main photo on the official website)
concept: A neighbourhood coworking space supporting women's first steps in business
OK Nishitokyo is presented as a facility supporting women's first steps in starting a business. It has three roles: coworking, a virtual office and a tourist information point for Nishitokyo City.
The entrance has a smartphone-operated auto-lock, and the lights and air conditioning can be controlled remotely. Welcome drinks such as coffee, tea and mineral water are provided.
steps: Three minutes from the South Exit of Tanashi Station
It is in room 201 of South Town, near Nishitokyo City's Tanashi office, in an area lined with the library and city offices.
Shared desks are monthly plans at ¥14,800 for one seat and ¥19,800 for two (excl. tax), with a minimum of three months.
Plans combined with address use come with a locker with a dedicated mailbox.
A photo from the prices page
Two meeting rooms for different uses
Meeting room B suits workshops, business meetings and web meetings. Meeting room A can be used for treatments, yoga, personal training and web meetings.
Both can be rented from one hour, at ¥1,000 per hour on weekdays and ¥1,300 on weekends and holidays.

word.title: What is a virtual office?
body: A service that lets you use a business address and mail handling without renting an actual desk.
At OK Nishitokyo, you can use the facility's address on business cards and post for ¥9,800 a month (excl. tax).

credits: Tanashi Coworking Space OK Nishitokyo official website: “Top”, “Prices”, “Access”

name: Coworking Space MONO
card: A makers' coworking space in Odaiba
title: Coworking Space MONO — a makers' coworking space directly linked to Telecom Center Station
lead: Coworking Space MONO is on the 14th floor of the Telecom Center Building East Wing, directly linked to Telecom Center Station. It is a coworking space for making things, where engineers, designers and start-ups gather, with a workshop equipped with a laser cutter, 3D printers and a CNC machine. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Directly linked to Telecom Center Station
Weekdays 10:00–18:00 (closed weekends and holidays); tenants 24 hours, 365 days
concept: An open-innovation platform for making things
MONO is presented as an “open innovation platform” where engineers, designers and start-ups gather.
With a workshop right next to where you work, you can build prototypes as you go. It also supports business development and hosts events for anywhere from a few people to about 300.
steps: The working space has power, Wi-Fi and free drinks. Drop-in is available in two-hour or full-day units during opening hours, 10:00–18:00 on weekdays.
The monthly coworking plan for weekdays is ¥6,000 (excl. tax).
The workshop has a laser cutter, 3D printers and a CNC machine. A news post also announced the addition of a Bambu Lab H2S 3D printer.
As well as meeting rooms, there is a nap room and a shower room. Tenant plans include private booths, private desks, free desks and private offices.
Tenants can use the facility 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and rent meeting rooms for ¥700 per hour (excl. tax).

word.title: What is a makerspace?
body: A place for making things, where machine tools such as 3D printers and laser cutters are shared.
MONO combines a coworking space with a workshop, bringing the places for working and prototyping together.

credits: © Coworking Space MONO (official website: top page)

name: Ota fab
card: A workshop with 15 3D printers, two minutes from Kamata Station
title: Ota fab — coworking with a maker workshop, two minutes from Kamata Station
lead: Ota fab is on the 6th floor of the Koyama No. 2 Building in Nishi-Kamata 7-chome, a two-minute walk from the West Exit of JR Kamata Station. Its roughly 200 m² floor brings together a coworking space, a fab lab with 3D printers and more, and rental space for meetings and lessons. In Ota City, known for its small factories, it is a place where work and making things share one space. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Kamata Station West Exit, 2 min walk
Weekdays 9:00–19:00, weekends & holidays 10:00–17:00 (open every day except New Year)
¥600/hour, ¥2,400 for the whole day after 3 hours (incl. tax)
concept: A digital community workshop next to where you work
Ota fab is a shared space run by Smile Link Co., Ltd., offering three uses: coworking, making things and rental space.

The fab lab is a community workshop with 3D printers, a laser cutter and a UV printer. Its users range from elementary-school children to people in their seventies, and it runs beginner workshops and programming classes for children.
steps: Choose from hourly drop-in to monthly fixed or free seats. Monthly plans are ¥30,800 for a fixed desk, ¥14,300 for a free desk and ¥5,500 for a weekend-and-holiday free desk.
There is free Wi-Fi, power at every seat and free drinks, and you can bring food in. There is a 34-inch ultra-wide monitor, and children are welcome.
A lounge for business talks, and meeting space
In the lounge space, you can invite clients for business talks, with free coffee and other drinks.

It also works as a venue for workshops and meetings, with a meeting area and whiteboards. Company registration and a dedicated mailbox are available, making it a base for starting a business or a side business.
There are 15 3D printers of four types, plus a laser cutter and a UV printer. Coworking members can use the Fab space as a development base.
Machine fees per hour are ¥600 for a 3D printer, ¥2,000 for the laser cutter and ¥2,700 for the UV printer.

word.title: What is a fab lab?
body: A workshop that opens digital machine tools such as 3D printers and laser cutters to the public.
At Ota fab, the fab lab is on the same floor as the coworking space, and members who have taken the training can use the machines.

name: Pointline YUTENJI
card: A lounge lined with books and a terrace, one minute from Yutenji Station
title: Pointline YUTENJI — a work lounge with books chosen by a bookshop, one minute from Yutenji Station
lead: Pointline YUTENJI is a six-storey creative office in Yutenji 2-chome, a one-minute walk from Yutenji Station on the Tokyu Toyoko Line. Floors 3–6 hold 20 office units, and the 6th floor has a meeting room, a work lounge and a rooftop terrace. Free desks are inside the work lounge, where you can read books selected by a bookshop. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Creative office, with free desks in the 6F work lounge
Tokyu Toyoko Line Yutenji Station, 1 min walk
Plan without company registration ¥25,000/month (¥27,500 incl. tax)
concept: People grow, the town grows
Pointline YUTENJI is an office developed by Tokyu Corporation, with planning, production and management by Real Gate Inc. Its motto is “people grow, the town grows”.
The ground floor holds a café, a drugstore and a supermarket, and the 2nd floor a nursery. Places for work and for daily life sit close together in one building.
steps: A lounge with books chosen by a bookshop
In the 6th-floor work lounge, you can read books selected by a bookshop. The book selection and Yutenji map were curated by the bookshop SUNNY BOY BOOKS.
It can be used for meetings and work, with Wi-Fi.
A paper collage of the neighbourhood
The ground-floor entrance lobby is decorated with a paper collage inspired by the scenery around Yutenji, and with design furniture.
A meeting room for 8 and a planted rooftop terrace
The 6th-floor meeting room holds up to 8 and has Wi-Fi.
The rooftop terrace, with planting and a wooden deck, looks out over Tokyo. Wi-Fi is available there too.

The free desks are inside the 6th-floor work lounge. The plan without company registration is ¥25,000 a month (¥27,500 incl. tax), without a company name display or dedicated mailbox. The plan with company registration is listed as full.
Equipment includes power outlets, Wi-Fi, a multifunction printer and a shredder.

word.title: What is a free desk?
body: A contract with no fixed seat, where you pick any free seat to use.
At Pointline YUTENJI, free desks are inside the 6th-floor work lounge and available by the month.

credits: Real Gate Inc. (planning, production, lessor and management) / developer: Tokyu Corporation
Pointline YUTENJI official website: top page
